IS : 3276.1966

Indian Standard
DIMENSIONS FOR MECHANICAL TURNING ARRANGEMENTS FOR STEEL COWL VENTILATORS 0. FOREWORD

0.1This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution

on 25 February 1966, after the draft finalized by the Marine Engineering and Shipbuilding Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council.

0.2 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on cowl ventilators. Other standards in the series are: IS : 3271-1966 detachable IS : 3272-1966 IS : 3273-1966 IS : 3275-1966 Genera1 requirements for steel cowl ventilators with components Dimensions for oval-head steel cowl ventilators Dimensions for circular-head steel cowl ventilators Dimensions for accessories for steel cow1 ventilators Dimensions for coamings for steel cowl ventilators IS : 3277(under preparation) IS : 3278-1966 .Dimensions for detachable coaming covers and wire mesh grids for steel cowl ventilators

0.3 In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from the following standards issued by the Association Francaise de Normalisation : NF 546-140 : 1951 Manches a air-commande par roues dent&s ensemble. (Ventilators-toothed wheel turning arrangementassembly) NF 546-144 : 1951 Manches a air-commande par roues denteescouronne et pignon. (Ventilators-toothed wheel turning arrangement--driving pinion) NF 546-146 : 1951 Manches a air-commande par roues dent&s ou par cardan-galet de guidage et tige de manoeuvre. (Ventilatorstoothed wheel turning arrangement control rod-details of guide roller and turning handle)

3

IS : 3276 - 1966 NF 546-148 : 1951 Manches a air-commande par roues dentiescrapaudine et pivot. (Ventilatorstoothed wheel turning arrangement, central guide tube and pivot bearings) NF 546-l 50 : 195 1 Manches a air-commande par roues denttescollier de fixation due tube de commande. (Ventilators-toothed wheel turning arrangement -fixing clamp and central guide tube) 0.4 Indian detachable standard. Standard general requirements components (IS : 3271-1966) for steel cowl ventilators with is a necessary adjunct to this

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, espresGng the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2- 1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

3.2 Method of Assembly -A ring, made in two or more sections (see Table l), with spur gear cut on its periphery, is fixed to the intermediate A driving pinion meshes with this ring and is trunking of the ventilator. The guide operated by a rod, fitted with handle to facilitate easy turning. roller assembly is fitted to the intermediate trunking in such a manner that In addition, the roller projects inwards through the intermediate trunking. in the case of large size ventilators, a central guide tube is fitted internally A pivot rod is attached with bearings attached to the intermediate trunking. to the bottom end of the guide tube and bears on a spherically seated washer, placed in the pivot bearing. The pivot bearing is placed centrally and Thus, with fitted on to the cross braces, which are welded to the coaming. the help of rollers and the guide tube, smooth operation of turning the ventilator is achieved.

* Rules for rounding off numerical values (r&).

,IS : 3276- 1966 3.2.1 U'heel and Pinion Arrangement - The wheel shall be bolted on to the angle iron by countersunk screws as shown in Fig. 3. The angle iron shall be riveted to intermediate trunking. The rivets shall be of 6 mm diameter and pitched at 48 mm. The dimensions of the wheel and pinion arrangement shall be as given in Table 1 and Fig. 3.
